nodes.name: Ramon (breadnut)
nodes.desc: One of the dominant trees of the Maya forest. Its fruits and seeds feed many animals, and birds and bats help spread the seeds.

nodes.name: Sapodilla
nodes.desc: A common forest tree of the Maya lowlands whose sweet fruit is eaten by fruit bats and other animals.

nodes.name: Kapok tree
nodes.desc: A giant emergent tree, sacred to the Maya. Fruit bats feed on its flowers and fruit.

nodes.name: Gumbo-limbo
nodes.desc: A common tree whose small fruits are eaten by many birds, bats and monkeys.

nodes.name: Geoffroy's spider monkey
nodes.desc: Fruit makes up most of its feeding time, with young leaves as the main extra. Jaguars and pumas are its main likely predators.

nodes.name: Central American agouti
nodes.desc: A ground rodent that eats fruit and seeds and stores seeds when food is plentiful, making it an important seed disperser.

nodes.name: Central American red brocket
nodes.desc: A small forest deer that browses leaves and picks up fallen fruit. It is a prey animal of the big cats.

nodes.name: Jamaican fruit bat
nodes.desc: Feeds on fruit of sapodilla, kapok, gumbo-limbo and other trees, carrying seeds as it flies.

nodes.name: Desmarest's spiny pocket mouse
nodes.desc: A small forest-floor rodent that eats seeds and fruit and is prey for snakes and small cats.

nodes.name: Ocellated turkey
nodes.desc: A ground-feeding omnivore of the Yucatan region eating insects such as leafcutter ants, plus seeds, nuts and leaves. It roosts high in trees, partly to avoid jaguars.

nodes.name: Keel-billed toucan
nodes.desc: A large-billed fruit eater of the canopy that spreads seeds of the trees it feeds on.

nodes.name: Leafcutter ants
nodes.desc: Common in the park. They cut leaves to feed a fungus garden and are themselves eaten by ocellated turkeys and coatis.

nodes.name: White-nosed coati
nodes.desc: An omnivore that forages on the ground and in trees for insects, small vertebrates, eggs, fruit and carrion.

nodes.name: Black vulture
nodes.desc: A scavenger that cleans up carcasses; GloBI records show it feeding on deer and agouti.

nodes.name: Terciopelo (fer-de-lance)
nodes.desc: A large venomous pit viper; GloBI records show it eating agoutis and climbing rats.

nodes.name: Ocelot
nodes.desc: A spotted cat that mostly hunts small mammals under about a kilogram, along with birds and reptiles. Jaguars and pumas can kill adults.

nodes.name: Jaguar
nodes.desc: The largest cat of the Americas and a top predator of the forest, taking deer, peccaries and other prey, including ocellated turkeys.

nodes.name: Puma
nodes.desc: A large cat that roams the park alongside the jaguar; spider monkeys are likely prey.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Year-round tropical light drives the growth of the forest canopy.

nodes.name: Wet-season rain
nodes.desc: The seasonal rains feed the forest and refill the low swampy ground.

nodes.name: Limestone ridges & soil
nodes.desc: The park sits on parallel limestone ridges above swampy lowlands, which shape where water and trees are.

nodes.name: Swampy lowlands
nodes.desc: Low wet ground between the limestone ridges where water collects and forest meets wetland.

nodes.name: Fungi & litter decomposers
nodes.desc: Break down fallen leaves, fruit and carcasses and return nutrients to the forest soil.
